doc.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017

title: Jazz parties, documentaries, 'jazz is dead' and closing
summary: They discuss declining jazz parties, new films, why jazz is declared dead, and close optimistically.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: The audience is not sort of fulfilling.
That’s a shame. And I don’t know about the jazz cruises. I don’t know if they’re still happening or not. I suppose once in a while.
Well I just talked to someone who went on an incredible jazz cruise. Like everybody was there.

Um hm. Well maybe that’s another way of getting out there. And hopefully what I hope will happen too is you know Carol Bash’s film, “The Lady Who Swings the Band” on Mary Lou Williams just came out, and of course it’s been a while since Ken Burns’ film on jazz came out. I think it’s time for another film like that, another documentary like that. And some gentleman came to me from some neat company in Europe and they did ask me questions for a film that they’re doing on jazz, which I hope will come out soon. So somebody else is doing something besides Ken Burns. And I hope there’ll be more projects like Carol Bash’s, “The Lady Who Swings the Band” and get that stuff out on television and so on. Like somebody once said, you know, you always hear jazz is dead, every ten years or something, whatever.
You know what I think about that, I think they need something to write about. When’s the last time anybody wrote jazz is dead? Okay, that was five years ago, it’s time to do it again.

Yeah exactly. I agree. But it’s not dead. It’s not dead. It’s alive. It may be on life support but it’s still there. It’s in good hands. And hopefully places like ours and yours, who have these institutes, will keep things going. You know, you’ve got a great web site, you’ve
got that YouTube channel which I’ve got to talk to you about actually, and YouTube, everything’s on YouTube now. It’s like —
Exactly. Exactly. So I think it’s in good hands. I think it’s in really good hands. I’m very optimistic.
And on that upbeat, thank you very much, it’s been a real pleasure.
Thanks, Monk. It was a pleasure talking to you.
